title: Simplify Path
prompt: Given an absolute file system path that starts with a slash, return its simplest form. Parts of the path are separated by one or more slashes. A part made of a single dot means the current folder and is dropped. A part made of two dots moves up to the parent folder, and at the top folder it stays there. Any other part, including three or more dots, is a folder name. The result starts with a single slash, separates folder names with single slashes, and has no slash at the end unless it is only the top folder.
